q: Pictured: tinsmith. Which vernacular term names it?
ref: Know-How Architecture, “Building Technology: Construction Vernacular Terms” (#InstaFlashCards): term and image.
n: “Latero” is the vernacular for tinsmith. Origin: Spanish latero “tinsmith”, from lata “tin plate, tin can”.

q: Pictured: stake. Which vernacular term names it?
ref: Know-How Architecture, “Building Technology: Construction Vernacular Terms” (#InstaFlashCards): term and image.
n: “Estaka” is the vernacular for stake. Origin: Spanish estaca “stake, post”.

q: Pictured: corner. Which vernacular term names it?
ref: Know-How Architecture, “Building Technology: Construction Vernacular Terms” (#InstaFlashCards): term and image.
n: “Kanto” is the vernacular for corner. Origin: Spanish canto “edge, corner”.

q: Pictured: foreman. Which vernacular term names it?
ref: Know-How Architecture, “Building Technology: Construction Vernacular Terms” (#InstaFlashCards): term and image.
n: “Kapatas, Maestro de Obra” is the vernacular for foreman. Origin: kapatas is Spanish capataz “foreman”; maestro de obra is “master of the works”.

q: Pictured: mason. Which vernacular term names it?
ref: Know-How Architecture, “Building Technology: Construction Vernacular Terms” (#InstaFlashCards): term and image.
n: “Kantero” is the vernacular for mason. Origin: Spanish cantero “stonemason”, from canto “stone, edge”.

q: Pictured: aligned. Which vernacular term names it?
ref: Know-How Architecture, “Building Technology: Construction Vernacular Terms” (#InstaFlashCards): term and image.
n: “Kalinya” is the vernacular for aligned. Origin: likely Spanish alinear or línea “line”: put into line.

q: Pictured: sketch plan. Which vernacular term names it?
ref: Know-How Architecture, “Building Technology: Construction Vernacular Terms” (#InstaFlashCards): term and image.
n: “Krokis” is the vernacular for sketch plan. Origin: croquis (French, also used in Spanish) “rough sketch”. It sounds like “croquis”.

q: Pictured: laying of chb. Which vernacular term names it?
ref: Know-How Architecture, “Building Technology: Construction Vernacular Terms” (#InstaFlashCards): term and image.
n: “Asinta” is the vernacular for laying of chb. Origin: likely Spanish asentar “to set in place”. Laying blocks means setting them on the wall.

q: Pictured: contractor. Which vernacular term names it?
ref: Know-How Architecture, “Building Technology: Construction Vernacular Terms” (#InstaFlashCards): term and image.
n: “Kontratista” is the vernacular for contractor. Origin: Spanish contratista, from contrato. Same root as English “contract”.

q: Pictured: alignment. Which vernacular term names it?
ref: Know-How Architecture, “Building Technology: Construction Vernacular Terms” (#InstaFlashCards): term and image.
n: “Asintada” is the vernacular for alignment. Origin: likely Spanish asentar “to set in place”. It describes setting work properly in line.

q: Pictured: plumb bob (plumbline). Which vernacular term names it?
ref: Know-How Architecture, “Building Technology: Construction Vernacular Terms” (#InstaFlashCards): term and image.
n: “Hulog” is the vernacular for plumb bob (plumbline). Origin: Tagalog hulog “to drop”. A plumb bob is dropped on a string.
